novel_mechanics_found: Solved L6's five-sprite grammar. The G-hook and n-glyph rotate through four ACTION5 orientations; the tall bar is a rigid two-marker connector; the three-marker arm stretches one marker horizontally by 3 pixels per press through columns 42,45,48,51 and ping-pongs; and the winding snake grows non-uniformly from 2 to 6 markers, sometimes extending only its black head/body before adding markers. Deselecting and reselecting the partially contracted snake appeared to reset or reverse its ping-pong direction: three presses then reached the six-marker maximum and completed the level, rather than the seven predicted from the prior traversal direction. A marker-constellation exact-cover search exposed a compact connected placement, with green feedback confirming each partial pair.
gotchas: Selected sprite shows markers (8s) and pairs show green (3); unselected sprites hide everything as color-4 bodies - survey by clicking each sprite before solving.

ACTION6 must hit non-transparent rendered sprite pixels; misses are no-ops that may tick the top bar. With overlapping sprites, pick pixels unique to the target (a mis-click selected the wrong sprite once and 11 moves dragged it away - fully recoverable by moving it back, pairs re-form automatically).

ACTION5 semantics are PER-SPRITE and PER-LEVEL: rigid 90-degree rotation on L4; variant-form cycling on L5+ (ping-pong through a form catalog, including ZERO-marker empty forms and length-growing snakes). Map each sprite cycle empirically (4-8 presses, positions of 8s and the 0 head).
The black 0-marker is the snake growth head, not a pairable marker; it vanishes at max length.

Solve analytically offline: catalog marker constellations per form, then constraint-solve (cover + cross-pair with per-sprite consistent translations, all on the 3px grid). The L5 catalog search had exactly ONE feasible configuration.
Sprite bodies may overlap freely; only marker coincidence matters.
Movement clamps at board edges (blocked moves waste an action and tick the bar).
The win fires instantly on the completing move - no validate action needed.

A transient all-green state on L5 did NOT fire the win once (subtle mis-pairing suspected after an accidental sprite displacement); rebuilding the identical config from scratch fired immediately - if all looks green with no win, tear one sprite away and re-place it.

L6 winning placement from the catalog state: max arm moves up 3 and left 4; initial G-hook moves right 3 and down 3; initial tall bar moves right 3 and up 3; initial n-glyph moves left 4 and down 3; reselect the winding snake and press ACTION5 three times to reach its max form and fire the win.
Selection appears to reset or reverse the winding snake's ping-pong direction; do not predict remaining presses solely from the direction observed before deselecting it.

The live win occurred at full-sequence action 279 (session env.step 691). Four queued post-terminal ACTION5 calls produced empty frames and reset reported levels_completed to 0, so the candidate sequence must end at action 279.

Only five calls remained, far short of the 279 needed for a fresh reproduce() gate, so this is an honestly live-observed but unverified replay candidate.
